cells.note: This quote is from the wiki entry rather than the supplied study text. The entry reports higher LD change scores at each interval, but the LD group remained substantially lower overall and did not catch up.

cells.quote: Word reading was an important source of reading comprehension difficulty for both groups. For non-ELs, the effect of word reading was larger than the effects of linguistic comprehension (vocabulary and listening comprehension combined); however, for ELs, the effects of linguistic comprehension were greater than the effect of word reading.
cells.note: The present study used multigroup structural equation modeling of measured skills rather than a treatment manipulation.

cells.quote: Vocabulary had indirect effects via both listening comprehension and word reading for ELs, but it demonstrated a direct effect on reading comprehension for non-ELs.
cells.note: The study reports different mediation mechanisms by learner group; no single printed effect size for this group contrast is given in the study text provided.

cells.quote: "for ELs, the complete mediation model where the effects of vocabulary were completely mediated by both listening comprehension and word reading was the most parsimonious and best fitting model (Δ𝜒2(1) = 1.11, p = .14; RMSEA [90% CI] = 0.04 [0.00, 0.07])."
cells.note: This sentence appears in the wiki entry but not in the supplied study-text excerpt; quote reproduced from the entry as instructed.
